name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 18 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch's status page, last updated 2 Jun, says the fourth global bleaching event likely ended in 2025, and no fifth event has been declared since (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report released on 31 Aug said another event was very likely given El Niño temperatures (bdnews24). Searches on 18 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so Normal holds with an upward trend.
for_you: Bleaching mainly affects reef ecosystems and the coastal communities that depend on them for fishing and tourism. Divers and visitors to tropical reefs may see bleached coral during marine heatwaves.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress per NOAA Coral Reef Watch (status page, 2 Jun)

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching: status update
bdnews24 — Global coral reefs get less time to recover as oceans heat up

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.

rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
